answer: A work-bonded reputation system makes Sybil attacks expensive: each agent must lock a refundable deposit and complete verifiable tasks before its attestations count. Like a vine, trust grows only along proven links, so a new identity starts with no weight and cannot borrow another's history. An oasis of trusted services can then require a minimum earned reputation and slash the deposit for fraud, so an attacker spawning thousands of clones must pay thousands of deposits and do thousands of jobs, while honest agents tend one garden of lasting identities.
